_comment: Hand-written homepage hero summaries, keyed by story slug. build-home-preview.mjs uses these instead of the automatic first sentence (HomepageStructure.heroDeck). Display only: story text is never changed. A finished first sentence is kept whole, up to about 60 words and past that without a mid-sentence ellipsis. Hand-written lines must end on a full stop and stay inside the story's own wording.

mantle-rock-and-the-trail-of-tears.heroDeck: Mantle Rock, a sandstone arch in Livingston County, stands near the old road that carried the Cherokee on the Trail of Tears in 1838–39.
mantle-rock-and-the-trail-of-tears.reason: Automatic clause cut gave 12 words ("West of the crossroads of Joy in Livingston County, off KY 133…"); Critiquito review of PR #191.

old-mulkey-meetinghouse-1804.heroDeck: South of Tompkinsville stands a log meetinghouse built in 1804 for the Mill Creek Baptist Church, pioneer Baptists from the Carolinas.
old-mulkey-meetinghouse-1804.reason: Automatic cut ended mid-sentence with an ellipsis ("…for the Mill Creek Baptist Church…"); editorial QA 2026-10-10.
